terra.problem: Papa describes opening his own mail, adding an unsupported detail to his world. Everyday things outside his bakery should be things people do.
The passage says access is into grace, not that access to someone is impossible when they are far away.
“That's a happy way to stand” is flat and adds little to the explanation.
The explanation repeats the answer but doesn't explain why Paul says to rejoice in sufferings. The comment about surprise doesn't explain the verse.
“Poured is a pouring word” is flat and doesn't add to the explanation.
The statement that prophets speak for God is a Bible fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
The reference to meeting an angel doesn't identify him as the angel who called Papa out of the drawer, leaving the backstory without its required context.
Paul's excitement is stated as a fact rather than Papa's impression, and the passage doesn't call justification the harder part.
The playful comment about the exclamation point makes the way Scripture is written the joke.
The comment about the exclamation point makes the way Scripture is written the setup for a joke.
The statement that offerings occur in the Bible refers to a fact outside this passage without a reference.
The statement about miracles in the Gospels refers to Bible events outside this passage without a reference.
Paul being an apostle is a Bible fact from outside this passage and needs a reference.
“The One we've now been reconciled to” follows Jesus Christ, but Paul says we are reconciled to God through Christ.
